10.0.s.en: 1. The killing of the sons of Saul on Mount Gilboa

10.0.0.en: 1 Now the Philistines fought against Israel; and the men of Israel fled from before the Philistines, and fell down slain in mount Gilboa. 2 And the Philistines followed hard after Saul, and after his sons; and the Philistines slew Jonathan, and Abinadab, and Malchishua, the sons of Saul.

10.0.1.en: Now the Philistines fought against Israel; and the men of Israel fled from before the Philistines, and fell down slain in mount Gilboa. [1]

10.1.0.en: After reviewing the genealogies, or the history of the children of Israel from creation to the Babylonian captivity (586 B.C.) in the preceding chapters, the writer returned to the period when the kingdom of Israel began. He did not begin with Saul’s receiving the kingship, but with his death, in order to bring us to the age of David, as the king whom God had chosen, who received a promise that his seed would reign forever. This was fulfilled by the coming of the King of kings, the Son of David, who reigns over our hearts eternally and raises up from His Church the Queen who sits at His right hand. Josephus, the Jewish historian, comments on what is said in this chapter [2], saying that since the writer opens his account of Saul the king with this battle, it is as though he wished to say that there was nothing good in the life of Saul worth mentioning on his behalf. He reigned for twenty years, as it were, without good fruit, and his life ended by his own hands, but with God’s permission, as though the Lord had killed him [14].

10.1.1.en: This period was one of the worst in the life of Israel, for the people insisted on appointing a king, which grieved the heart of Samuel the prophet (1 Sam 8:6). Although victories were achieved over some of the nations, the king sinned, and instead of repenting of his sins, what concerned him was his personal honor before the people. So his life ended with the people falling, together with their king, before the Philistines. It is as though the outcome of the people’s insistence on appointing a king like the other nations, and of Saul’s insistence on his own honor, was destruction for the king and the people!

10.2.0.en: v What madness! Does this proud man not know that his glory vanishes and evaporates like a dream, and that greatness and authority are nothing but a deceptive mirage [3].

10.3.0.en: v The Pharisee prayed with himself and not with God, because the sin of pride turned him back to himself [4].

10.4.0.en: v He must not glorify himself nor utter anything that praises himself, nor find pleasure in listening to another’s praise of him, but serve in everything in secret, not working for the sake of appearance before men, but seeking the praise of God alone, and contemplating His glorious and awesome coming, as well as his own departure from this world, and the blessings prepared for the righteous and the fire prepared for the devil and his angels (Mt 25:41) [5].

10.4.1.en: St. Basil the Great What occupied the heart of the people was temporal things and not the Kingdom of God, so they received a king according to the desire of their hearts, a lover of temporal honor, and so he and his people lost both the temporal and the eternal.

10.5.0.en: St. Basil the Great sees that the work of the serpent, that is, Satan, is to corrupt our nature, so that we no longer look upward but bow down like the animals toward the dust, seeking earthly things. Therefore he advises us, saying: [The head of the beasts looks toward the earth, but the head of man was created to look toward heaven, and his eyes are directed upward. Therefore it is fitting for us to seek the things that are above, and with our insight to pierce through earthly things [6].]

10.6.0.en: And the Philistines followed hard after Saul, and after his sons; and the Philistines slew Jonathan, and Abinadab, and Malchishua, the sons of Saul. [2]

10.6.1.en: King Saul sinned, so disaster fell upon the people, and his sons also reaped the fruit of their father’s deeds.

10.6.2.en: Many are often astonished and ask: What fault is it of the people? And what crime have the sons committed? God allows this not in order to punish the people because of the sins of the leader, nor the sons because of the fathers, but in order to urge the people, as well as the sons, not to go astray after the errors of leaders and parents. This is what the Lord Christ affirms in saying: “He that loveth father or mother more than me is not worthy of me” (Mt 10:37).

10.7.0.en: v The Holy Scripture commands us to obey our parents. Yes, but whoever loves them more than Christ loses his soul. Behold, the enemy (who persecutes me so that I may deny Christ) carries a sword to kill me; shall I then think of my mother’s tears? Or shall I despise the service of Christ for the sake of a father, whose burial I am not bound to attend if I am a servant of Christ (Lk 9:59-60), even though, as a true servant of Christ, I owe this (burial) to all [7].

10.8.s.en: 2. The suicide of Saul on Mount Gilboa

10.8.0.en: 3 And the battle went sore against Saul, and the archers hit him, and he was wounded of the archers. 4 Then said Saul to his armourbearer, “Draw thy sword, and thrust me through therewith; lest these uncircumcised come and abuse me.” But his armourbearer would not; for he was sore afraid. So Saul took a sword, and fell upon it. 5 And when his armourbearer saw that Saul was dead, he fell likewise on the sword, and died. 6 So Saul died, and his three sons, and all his house died together. 7 And when all the men of Israel that were in the valley saw that they fled, and that Saul and his sons were dead, then they forsook their cities, and fled: and the Philistines came and dwelt in them.

10.8.1.en: And the battle went sore against Saul, and the archers hit him, and he was wounded of the archers. [3]

10.8.2.en: Saul abused the longsuffering of God, and thought that as a king possessing authority he was not subject to the law, and that there was no one to stand before him and call him to account. But divine justice overtook him and confronted him at the appropriate time, so his authority was taken from him, his family lost its dignity as a royal house, and David, the persecuted one, received the throne.

10.9.0.en: v Many very negligent persons use God’s compassion as a pretext to increase the guilt of their sins, and carry their negligence to excess, saying thus: “There is no hell, there is no coming punishment. God forgives us all our sins.” To stop their mouths the wise man says: “Say not, His mercy is great; he will forgive the multitude of my sins” (Sir 5:6), and also: [As His mercy is great, so is His correction also] (Sir 16:12) [8].

10.10.0.en: v Now if the laws of men are observed with care, how much more is this required for the laws of God. A man says: “But He is good.” How long shall we utter this folly? I say folly, not because God is not good, but because he thinks of His goodness in order to achieve this end... Listen to the Holy Scripture, which says: “Say not, His mercy is great; he will forgive the multitude of my sins” (Sir 5:6). He did not command us to say: “His mercy is great.” He does not enjoin us this, but rather He wants us to say this always, and with the following purpose, which the Apostle Paul raises with every kind of proof. He means: Do not marvel at the compassions of God so that you sin and say: “His mercy removes the multitude of my sins”... but rather that we may not despair because of our sins, but repent, for “the goodness of God leadeth thee to repentance” (Rom 2:4), not to a greater evil [9].

10.11.0.en: St. John Chrysostom v (The Lord) says through the mouth of the prophet: [My son, add not sin unto sin and say, The mercy of God is great] (Sir 5:5-6). “Not knowing that the goodness of God leadeth thee to repentance” (Rom 2:4). For who is as merciful as God, who forgives all the sins of those who return to Him, and makes the wild olive tree a partaker of the fatness of the olive tree; and likewise who is as strict as He, so that He breaks off the natural branches because of their unbelief? (Rom 11:17-24) [10].

10.11.1.en: St. Augustine More than once Saul aimed his spear at David to kill him, but the spear did not reach David, because the Lord preserved him for the purity of his heart. But as for King Saul, when one of the soldiers aimed his spear at him, he struck him at once with a serious wound, as though he drank from the cup that he had filled to give David to drink.

10.12.0.en: Then said Saul to his armourbearer,

10.12.1.en: “Draw thy sword, and thrust me through therewith; lest these uncircumcised come and abuse me.”

10.12.2.en: But his armourbearer would not; for he was sore afraid.

10.12.3.en: So Saul took a sword, and fell upon it. [4]

10.12.4.en: Here we notice the following in the situation of the wounded Saul:

10.12.5.en: A. Saul realized that the more he strove with all his effort to obtain temporal honor, the more, when he fell into the hands of the Philistines, he would receive bitter insults. Thus those who hold honors, or who love great honors, are exposed to the danger of being exposed to scandal and mockery.

10.12.6.en: B. Whoever does not give glory to God in his success, the unbelievers can dominate him and make a public spectacle of his corpse.

10.12.7.en: C. Since Saul disobeyed the divine commandment more than once, even in the moments of his death he asked his armourbearer to draw his sword and kill him, so that the enemy would not mock him, but he did not listen to him; rather he disobeyed him.

10.13.0.en: And when his armourbearer saw that Saul was dead, he fell likewise on the sword, and died. [5]

10.14.0.en: So Saul died, and his three sons, and all his house died together. [6]

10.14.1.en: Saul and his sons and all his house thought that they were a royal family with an inviolability that no one could touch, but behold, they fell under judgment in a single day, all at once.

10.15.0.en: And when all the men of Israel that were in the valley saw that they fled, and that Saul and his sons were dead, then they forsook their cities, and fled: and the Philistines came and dwelt in them. [7]

10.15.1.en: By faith Israel enjoyed the Promised Land in a spirit of victory, strength and success, but through sin they lost much, and destruction befell them.

10.16.s.en: 3. The public disgrace and mockery of Saul and his sons

10.16.0.en: 8 And it came to pass on the morrow, when the Philistines came to strip the slain, that they found Saul and his sons fallen in mount Gilboa. 9 And when they had stripped him, they took his head, and his armour, and sent into the land of the Philistines round about, to carry tidings unto their idols, and to the people. 10 And they put his armour in the house of their gods, and fastened his head in the temple of Dagon.

10.16.1.en: And it came to pass on the morrow, when the Philistines came to strip the slain, that they found Saul and his sons fallen in mount Gilboa. [8]

10.17.0.en: And when they had stripped him, they took his head, and his armour, and sent into the land of the Philistines round about, to carry tidings unto their idols, and to the people. [9]

10.18.0.en: The Hindus practice such a custom: when they triumph over their enemies they carry the good news to their idols with a great celebration and procession [11].

10.19.0.en: And they put his armour in the house of their gods, and fastened his head in the temple of Dagon. [10]

10.19.1.en: Dagon: one of the most important gods of the Philistines, whom they believed to be the god who sends the rain and supplies them with abundant crops. Therefore they built temples for him wherever they settled in a land in Canaan where grain is grown. When drought came they cried out to him to send them rain. And if distress became severe they offered their children to him as sacrifices to appease him, and they used the temples to humiliate captives and to make a public spectacle of them by every means, as a kind of entertainment and glorification of Dagon (Judg 16:23-30), reckoning in this an honoring of the idols and an acknowledgment of their power.

10.20.s.en: 4. The men of Jabesh-gilead bury the bones of Saul and his sons

10.20.0.en: And when all Jabesh-gilead heard all that the Philistines had done to Saul, [11]

10.21.0.en: They arose, all the valiant men, and took away the body of Saul, and the bodies of his sons, and brought them to Jabesh, and buried their bones under the oak in Jabesh, and fasted seven days. [12]

10.21.1.en: The valiant men of Jabesh-gilead had not forgotten that Saul had earlier rescued their city (1 Sam 11), so they wished to repay his good deed after his death.

10.21.2.en: Although God had permitted the chastening of Saul even in the manner of his death, He permitted the heroes of Jabesh-gilead to take the bodies of Saul and his sons and carry them to Jabesh. For despite the faults and evils of Saul and his sons, they felt bound to honor him and his sons as their leaders even after their death and the abuse done to them. So it is fitting for the believer to give honor to whom honor is due, whether in the Church, at work, in the state, or in the army (1 Thess 5:12-13; Rom 13:1-7).

10.21.3.en: Likewise David the prophet bore no feelings of revenge or gloating toward Saul, who bore bitter enmity toward him without cause.

10.22.0.en: 13 So Saul died for his transgression which he committed against the LORD, even against the word of the LORD, which he kept not, and also for asking counsel of one that had a familiar spirit, to enquire of it; 14 And enquired not of the LORD: therefore he slew him, and turned the kingdom unto David the son of Jesse.

10.22.1.en: So Saul died for his transgression which he committed against the LORD, even against the word of the LORD, which he kept not.

10.22.2.en: And also for asking counsel of one that had a familiar spirit, to enquire of it; [13]

10.22.3.en: He gave two reasons for his death. First, Saul sinned by his disobedience to the Lord. He did not keep the word of the Lord (1 Sam 13; 15). Saul was condemned for his lack of faithfulness to the word of the Lord. This ingratitude, sadly, was the mark of all the kings of Israel (the northern kingdom) and some of the kings of Judah.

10.22.4.en: Second: by his turning to the familiar spirit to seek counsel instead of turning to God (1 Sam 28). The writer considers that Saul’s resort to divination, rather than turning to God, corrupted every aspect of his life.

10.23.0.en: And enquired not of the LORD: therefore he slew him, and turned the kingdom unto David the son of Jesse. [14]

10.23.1.en: Saul had earlier sought God’s guidance (1 Sam 28:5-6), but here he did not seek His guidance.

10.23.2.en: This contradiction reveals what was in Saul’s heart. Although he had earlier sought God’s guidance, it was when he had no other means before him. And perhaps when he sought God he did so in a deadly literalism, without trust in God or true reliance. For Saul was known for his selfishness, seeking his own personal glory and popularity and not the glory of God, and he was marked by a spirit of stubbornness and constant rebellion.

10.23.3.en: David was given many opportunities to be rid of Saul (1 Sam 31:3-4), but he did not stretch out his hand against the Lord’s anointed, despite God’s promise to him of receiving the throne; and when Saul died he wept for him and lamented him with all love and sincerity, without haste to take up the rule.

10.23.4.en: David did not hasten to seize the throne, although he knew that God had rejected Saul and had chosen him as king. In patience and expectation of the work of God, and in complete surrender into His hands, he did not hasten events, so that he might receive the throne from the hand of God at the appropriate time.

10.23.5.en: “Therefore he slew him,” although it was he himself who put an end to his own life (1 Sam 31:3-4). Because of his continual stubbornness and rebellion (1 Sam 15:22-23), the grace of God forsook him and left him to carry out his evil will, so he killed himself by his own will.

10.24.s.en: The death of Saul and the rising of the new man

10.24.0.en: The end of King Saul represents the old carnal man, who must die, and King David takes his place, representing the new spiritual man who is in the image of his Creator. As the Apostle Paul says: “That ye put off concerning the former conversation the old man, which is corrupt according to the deceitful lusts; and be renewed in the spirit of your mind; and that ye put on the new man, which after God is created in righteousness and true holiness” (Eph 4:22-24).

10.24.1.en: v [The king’s daughter is all glorious within] (Ps 45:13)... The man who joins himself to the love of the Father who sees in secret (Mt 6:6), and prays and works without his aim being the glory of men but the glory of God (Mt 6:10), is like the king’s daughter, all his glory being within. Do not look for garments fitting for one who is in the image of the Creator, as the Apostle says: “Seeing that ye have put off the old man with his deeds; and have put on the new man, which is renewed in knowledge after the image of him that created him” (Col 3:9-10), “Put on therefore, as the elect of God, holy and beloved, bowels of mercies, kindness, humbleness of mind, meekness, longsuffering” (Col 3:12). Such a man is adorned from within, in his inner man. The Apostle also urges us [to put on the Lord Jesus Christ] (Rom 13:14), not in our outward man, but so that the thought of God may wholly take control of our thought. But I believe that the woven spiritual garments are woven by the building word, especially if it is accompanied by positive work. Also, just as garments are woven on a loom, in which the threads are interlaced, so it is with the word accompanied by positive work; it resembles the holy garment of the soul that is filled with sayings of virtue and the doing of them [12].

10.24.2.en: v [Sing unto the Lord a new song; play skilfully on the harp to honor Him] (Ps 33:3). Sing unto the Lord a truly new song, that is, worship the Lord, [not in the oldness of the letter, but in newness of spirit] (Rom 7:6).

10.24.3.en: The man who does not understand the Law in a literal way, but grasps it with a spiritual understanding, is able to sing a new song, for the Old Testament has grown old and passed away, and the new song, renewed by the teachings of the Lord, has appeared to us. He is the one who renews our youth like the eagle’s (Ps 103:5), “though our outward man perish, yet the inward man is renewed day by day” (2 Cor 4:16), and the one who [reaches forth unto those things which are before] (Phil 3:13) is renewed more and more. And the one who is renewed prays to God always a truly new song.

10.24.4.en: Truly the expression “new” is applied to something exceptional and recent. When you describe the Incarnation of the Lord, which surpasses all nature, you are singing a new and unusual song. And when you explain the birth of the world and its complete renewal, after it had grown old through sin, the new birth that renewed it with a thorough renewal, you are singing a truly new song. Likewise when you speak of the Resurrection, you are singing a truly new and recent song [13].

10.24.6.en: Let my old man die, and let my new man rise in Your image!

10.24.7.en: v In the waters of Baptism You crucified my old man with all his lusts.

10.24.8.en: And You granted me the new man who is in Your image.

10.24.9.en: Grant me that with every day my old man may be crucified with all his deeds.

10.24.10.en: Make sin bitter in my mouth, so that I may not desire it nor be enslaved to it.

10.24.11.en: With every morning let me cling to You the more, that Your splendor may shine upon my mind, my heart and all my senses.

10.24.12.en: Let me be counted in truth a member of Your body, O Son of David.

10.24.13.en: v Let Saul die, and his sons and all the people of his house.

10.24.14.en: May You shatter all corruption within me, and let David live and reign in my heart.

10.24.15.en: You establish Your Kingdom within me, so that I enjoy royal authority even over my thoughts.

10.24.16.en: You remove from me all that is foreign to You.

10.24.17.en: And You grant me to become in truth Your holy Jerusalem.

10.24.18.en: v Come, O Son of David and his Lord, and reveal Your glory within me!

10.24.19.en: Then my depths will become a new heaven, into which no corruption or sin will creep.

10.24.20.en: But it will be renewed with every morning, and my soul will rejoice in You!
